page: Microsoft Azure E16a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Hardware resources include 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local ephemeral storage is bundled with a capacity of 410 GB, while dedicated GPU hardware is absent. The virtualization layer is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a balanced performance profile with specific architectural tradeoffs. The single-core processing capabilities are relatively constrained, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 768.29, placing it in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales effectively, achieving an average multi-core stress-ng score of 6102.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8135.0. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by an average read-only small block bandwidth of 795.44 GB/sec, though large-block write operations exhibit weaker throughput at 25.51 GB/sec. Database operations and key-value store performance are stable, with Redis SET operations averaging 14.24 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16a_v4 offers a high density of memory relative to compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require top-tier single-thread CPU performance. The inclusion of 410 GB of local storage adds value for workloads requiring temporary scratch space. This virtual machine is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, data processing tasks, and moderate web serving operations.
